newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy faces chaotic two weeks of transport strikes.
newsitem.headline: Italy faces chaotic two weeks of transport strikes.

text.p: Air traffic controllers went on strike at 11 Italian airports Monday at the start of what is expected to be two chaotic weeks of stoppages by transport workers locked in contract disputes.

The eight-hour stoppage at Bari, Bologna, Cagliari, Catania, Genoa, Milan Malpensa, Naples, Bergamo, Palermo, Trieste and Turin had little effect on traffic since it was called by smaller controllers' unions.
But big delays were expected as a result of another planned eight-hour air traffic controllers' strike Wednesday called by six main labour organisations.
Transport Minister Claudio Burlando was to meet representatives of air traffic controllers' unions later Monday to try and avert further strike action.
Another meeting was set for Tuesday with rail workers who have called a 24-hour stoppage from the evening of April 19.
"We are working to change what was a truce into a long-term agreement on a plan to change the Italian transport system, which is at the moment far behind other countries," he said.
Further national stoppages by bus, tram and metro drivers were planned for Thursday, followed next Monday by a four-day strike by gas station attendants.
Another strike by air traffic controllers was planned in Milan for Friday April 18 and a four-day sea transport strike was due to start April 19.
